extracted.intended_audience: hospital coders, medical device manufacturers, Medicare policy stakeholders, health services researchers, and other commenters on IPPS/LTCH PPS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, data tests, and analytic considerations CMS uses to evaluate requests to reassign cases or to create/split MS-DRGs (including GROUPER cluster logic, case counts, cost/LOS comparisons, and subgroup-creation criteria). Intended to guide CMS rulemaking and public comment analysis for IPPS/LTCH MS-DRG changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: MDC assignment based on diagnosis codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnosis codes describing certain conditions (for example, spinal deformities, degenerative conditions, sacroiliac joint dysfunction, degenerative sacroiliitis) are assigned to a Major Diagnostic Category (MDC 08 in these examples), and therefore cases reporting the related procedure codes are expected to group to the MDC 08 MS-DRGs instead of to MDC 01 MS-DRGs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating reassignment requests, verify the principal/secondary diagnosis mapping to MDCs (see ICD-10 MS-DRG Definitions Manual Version 43.1 and later) because the MDC assignment governs expected MS-DRG grouping.

rubrics_metrics.name: GROUPER cluster logic and restricted clusters
rubrics_metrics.description: The GROUPER program identifies collections of ICD-10-PCS procedure codes called clusters; clusters may have a different set of attributes than their component codes and may be 'restricted' by MDC, which inhibits use of the component codes' attributes for MS-DRG assignment logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: codes 0SPC0JZ and 0SRT0JZ together create cluster @0045 whose attributes (and possibly restrictions for MDC 08) determine grouping rather than the individual codes. Analysts must examine cluster behavior (including restrictions) when reconciling shifts in case volumes and grouping outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgical/hierarchy logic consistency for MS-DRG reassignment
rubrics_metrics.description: MS-DRGs are defined by specific surgical definitions (for example, MS-DRG 402 defined by single level combined anterior and posterior spinal fusion; MS-DRG 428 defined by multiple level combined anterior and posterior spinal fusion), and reassignment of cases must be consistent with the intended clinical/surgical differentiation embodied in MS-DRG logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to reassign cases must respect the clinical definitions and aims of MS-DRG differentiation (e.g., single vs multiple level combined fusions are clinically distinct and resource-differentiated), so reassignments that contradict those definitions are not feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup-creation criterion: minimum case counts (>= 500 per severity group)
rubrics_metrics.description: One criterion to split a base MS-DRG into severity level subgroups is having at least 500 cases in each of the proposed MCC, with CC, and without CC/MCC groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS applies this numerical threshold when assessing whether a base MS-DRG can be subdivided; the test must be satisfied in the analytic dataset (e.g., MedPAR update) used for the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup-creation criterion: minimum percentage share (>= 5% per severity group)
rubrics_metrics.description: Another criterion for splitting is that each proposed severity group (MCC, CC, without CC/MCC) must represent at least 5 percent of the cases in the base MS-DRG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures each subgroup is not only numerically sufficient but also represents a meaningful share of the base MS-DRG caseload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup-creation criterion: relative cost difference (>= 20% between groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 20 percent difference in average costs between the MCC group, the CC group, and the without CC/MCC group is required to justify a split.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses this relative cost threshold to establish that severity-level splits materially differentiate expected resource use across groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup-creation criterion: absolute cost difference (>= $2,000 between groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to percent differences, there must be at least a $2,000 difference in average costs between the severity groups being compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This absolute-dollar threshold complements the percent test to ensure practical payment relevance of the split.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup-creation criterion: reduction in cost variance (>= 3% improvement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed severity splits must produce at least a 3 percent reduction in cost variance (indicating increased explanatory power of the base MS-DRG for expected cost) compared to not splitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statistical/explanatory-power test shows that the severity-level split improves the accuracy of the payment system by capturing differences in expected cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: All five subgroup criteria must be met to split a base MS-DRG
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with CMS' established process, once the decision is made to propose further modifications such as creating a new base MS-DRG, all five criteria (case counts, percent share, 20% cost difference, $2,000 cost difference, >=3% variance reduction) must be satisfied for the base MS-DRG to be subdivided by CC/MCC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses proposing splits must demonstrate compliance with each of the five tests in the supplied tables and underlying datasets before CMS will finalize subgroup splits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect existing severity subdivision structure when considering reassignment
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot reassign cases into a severity level subgroup if the target MS-DRG is a base MS-DRG that is not subdivided (for example, MS-DRG 402 is a base MS-DRG and is not subdivided into severity levels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requestors must consider whether the target MS-DRG has existing severity level splits; moving cases between base (unsplit) and split MS-DRGs may be infeasible or inconsistent with grouper logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of average cost and average length of stay (LOS) comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS examines average costs and average length of stay for cases reporting the device/procedure/condition of interest versus the averages for 'all cases' in the respective MS-DRG and across severity levels to assess whether resource use and LOS differ materially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher average costs and comparable/longer LOS for the target cases relative to all cases in an MS-DRG support consideration of reassignment or creation of a new MS-DRG; small or inconsistent differences argue against reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of clinical distinctiveness and device indications
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS considers whether the device/procedure is indicated for different clinical populations or more complex procedures (for example, aprevo® indicated for adults with spinal deformities and degenerative conditions; iFuse Bedrock for sacroiliac joint dysfunction) and whether those differences imply different resource utilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical distinctiveness that maps to higher resource use supports separate grouping; CMS evaluates indications, typical procedures, and clinical complexity as part of rationale for grouping changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of procedure code setting (O.R. vs non-O.R.) and primary driver of resource use
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS notes whether a procedure code is designated operating room (O.R.) or non-operating room (non-O.R.) (for example, the insertion of a bone void filler XW0V0P7 is designated non-O.R.) and whether other clinical factors (such as infection) are the key drivers of resource utilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a procedure is non-O.R., CMS evaluates whether associated clinical conditions (e.g., periprosthetic joint infection) drive resource use and thus whether reassignment to higher severity MS-DRG is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for overlapping procedure codes and cluster restrictions before finalizing changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlap among procedure codes and cluster restrictions (or removal thereof) can redistribute cases across MS-DRGs and affect whether MS-DRGs meet subgroup criteria; CMS identified overlaps that impacted grouping when restriction logic was removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts should examine code overlaps and cluster restrictions in the GROUPER (and simulate effects of removing restrictions) because such behavior can materially change case counts and cost statistics used to justify splits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of test GROUPER versions and public documentation for analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS makes test versions of the ICD-10 MS-DRG GROUPER software (e.g., Version 43, Version 44) and draft Definitions Manuals publicly available so stakeholders can analyze the impact of proposed changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders should use the publicly available test GROUPER and draft Definitions Manual to validate grouping, reconcile shifts, and prepare comments; CMS will reference the test GROUPER results in rulemaking analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of procedure code updates and incorporation into final materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure code proposals finalized after the Spring update will be footnoted in final rule tables (Table 6B, Table 6F) with MDC, MS-DRG assignments, and O.R./non-O.R. designations; public feedback on final assignments may be considered for the following fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or requesting changes, consider the code update timeline and that final code decisions may appear only in the final rule with footnotes; plan comments accordingly (deadlines such as April 17, 2026 for Spring 2026 updates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider distribution across severity levels when evaluating reassignment impact
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS evaluates whether reassigning lower severity cases to higher severity levels would leave unaddressed cases at the MCC level that still have higher costs/LOS, noting that moving some cases upward does not resolve remaining high-cost MCC cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses should show how reassignment affects all severity levels and whether reassignment would appropriately account for MCC-level cases; inability to reassign MCC cases can argue against simple upward reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard for proposing a new base MS-DRG
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes creating a new base MS-DRG when analyses demonstrate that cases (e.g., extensive fusions or complex fusion procedures using specified devices) show increased resource utilization, higher average costs, and different LOS compared to existing MS-DRGs and when subgroup-creation criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should present comprehensive data on counts, cost, LOS, severity-level distribution, and how the new base MS-DRG and subsequent severity splits would improve payment accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and definition revision when reassigning/creating MS-DRGs
rubrics_metrics.description: When CMS reassigns cases to new MS-DRGs, it may also revise existing MS-DRG titles to remove device-specific references (for example, removing 'Custom-made Anatomically Designed Interbody Fusion Device' or 'Extensive Fusions' from certain MS-DRG titles) to reflect updated grouping logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders should review proposed title/definition revisions because they reflect the intended scope of the MS-DRG and affect interpretation for coding and reimbursement.
